            "project_id": "X26-RB10",
            "answer_text": "Our campus stands out because it combines a strong sense of community, purpose‑driven learning, and spaces designed for growth—both academically and personally.\n\n\nPeople-first culture\nStudents, faculty, and staff know each other by name. This supportive environment makes it easier to ask questions, collaborate, and feel like you truly belong.\n\n\nHands-on, real-world learning\nClasses are designed to go beyond theory, emphasizing practical experience, teamwork, and problem-solving that prepare students for real careers and life beyond campus.\n\n\nAccessible and supportive resources\nFrom tutoring and mentoring to wellness and career services, support is easy to find and tailored to individual needs.\n\n\nCampus spaces that inspire\nWhether it’s modern labs, quiet study areas, green spaces, or gathering spots, the campus is built to encourage focus, creativity, and connection.\n\n\nOpportunities to get involved\nClubs, organizations, service projects, and leadership roles allow students to explore interests, build confidence, and make an impact.\n\n\nA shared sense of purpose\nWhat truly makes the campus special isn’t just the buildings—it’s the shared commitment to growth, respect, and continuous improvement.",

            "project_id": "X26-RB10",
            "answer_text": "The overall maintenance and cleanliness of certain buildings, including the library, appear inconsistent when compared to others on campus. A more standardized approach to facilities upkeep would help ensure an equitable and professional environment across all spaces.\n\nIn terms of landscaping, the current approach seems to rely on seasonal plantings that require frequent replacement. Transitioning to more sustainable, lower-maintenance, and climate-appropriate landscaping could improve both cost efficiency and long-term aesthetics, while a more naturalized design may better align with current best practices.\n\nEnhancing wayfinding, lighting, and overall accessibility should also be a priority. Ensuring clear signage and well-lit, accessible pathways would significantly improve usability, safety, and the overall student experience.\n\nAdditionally, drainage remains a concern in several areas, as sidewalks and walking paths are prone to flooding during rain.             "project_id": "X26-RB10",
            "answer_text": "The vending machines and bookstore pricing are too high.
